Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a compact Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on evaluation success criteria and a proposed close cadence. I want to make sure we are aligned on the minimal acceptance bar so your team can validate quickly without over-indexing on low-value tests.

Key highlights (TL;DR):
- Goal: Verify Redwood inference meets 99th percentile latency target and 95% accuracy-equivalence on your NLU test set under representative traffic.
- Exit gates: perf SLOs met in dedicated sandbox, reproducible quality on the shared prompt suite, and security checklist (SOC2 scoping) completed.
- Acceptance tests: latency/throughput benchmarks (three load profiles), quality A/B on 10k utterances, and an integration smoke test for VPC routing.
- Timeline proposal: 3-week evaluation window + 1 week for post-eval wrap and contracting.

I've attached the MAP spreadsheet and an evaluation test matrix. Please review and flag anything you want tightened or loosened. If this looks reasonable, can we lock the kickoff for Monday 2026-10-12?

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman

Hi Liam / Aisha —

Thanks Liam — great questions. Quick answers and an operational proposal below.

Metric definition
- Primary quality metric: macro-averaged F1 on Hearth Tech's canonical intent and entity labels (we used your sample corpus schema in the attached test matrix). This avoids class imbalance issues and matches how your models are evaluated today.
- Secondary: end-to-end intent accuracy for the top intent per utterance (used for executive reporting).

Acceptance test specifics (from the eval_test_matrix_HEARTH.csv):
- Functional/quality: run the shared 10k utterance suite across Redwood (production-sized model) and your baseline model; pass if macro F1 delta <= 5 points and no systematic label regressions on the top 5 intents.
- Latency: three load profiles
  * Baseline (dev): 5 concurrent users, 1–2 requests/s — median P95 < 220ms
  * Steady-state (pilot): 200 concurrent users, 25 requests/s — median P95 < 450ms
  * Spike (stress): 500 concurrent users, burst 75 requests/s — 99th percentile < 900ms with graceful degradation policy enabled
- Stability: KV cache hit-rate >= 70% for long-running sessions (per your session distribution)
- Security: SOC2 scoping questionnaire answers + evidence pack (audit log sample, KMS integration snapshot) delivered 72 hours prior to kickoff.

Proposal for dates and activities
- Kickoff: 2026-10-26 — alignment call (30 min) to review test harness and keys.
- Week 1 (10/27–11/02): Integration & smoke testing (VPC peering, sample inference runs).
- Week 2 (11/03–11/09): Controlled load tests and quality runs against 10k suite.
- Week 3 (11/10–11/16): Spike/stress tests and regression analysis; iterate on tuning.
- Wrap (11/17–11/20): Final report, decision call, signoff or list of follow-ups.

If those windows look okay, we will update the attached MAP spreadsheet with the locked dates and contact owners for each test. Sean and Dev — please confirm infra readiness for the proposed load profiles and the expected cost estimate so we can share it with Hearth.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
